answer: Sequential challenge lineage: each identity must solve a unique challenge derived from the prior block's answer, submitted within a short window. The rule rejects any reply whose hash matches an earlier one, forcing fresh computation per identity and making bulk replication fail at the marble checkpoint. An attacker's cost scales with distinct compute per identity, not shared work, pushing marginal cost toward the zenith of honest single-node effort. A failed submission forfeits the plume of accumulated priority, so farms lose standing faster than they gain it.
